report.sources_described: Surface water from Los Gatos Creek (source 004_004), treated by conventional surface water treatment; the drinking water source assessment is available by request.
violations: Tables 7, 9 and 11 (violations) all read 'None'.

Page 8 disclosure (State Revised Total Coliform Rule): 'Although E.coli was detected during routine sampling, the water system was not in violation of the E.coli MCL. An E.coli MCL violation only occurs if one of the following conditions is met - E.coli-positive repeat sample following TC-positive routine sample, TC-positive repeat sample following an E.coli positive routine sample, failure to collect all required repeat samples following a E.coli-positive routine sample, or failure to test for E.coli when any repeat sample is TC-positive.' (Table 1 nonetheless prints 0 E. coli detections.)

Page 8 disclosure (chromium 6): 'chromium (hexavalent) was detected at levels that exceed the chromium (hexavalent) MCL. While a water system of our size is not considered in violation of the chromium (hexavalent) MCL until after October 1st, 2028, we are working to address this exceedance and comply with the MCL. Specifically, we are conducting quarterly Chromium-6 sampling to monitor the contamination, and are investigating possible feasible treatment options to comply with the MCL compliance date.' (Table 4 nonetheless prints 0.25 ppb against the 10 ppb MCL.)

report.title: 2025 Consumer Confidence Report - Chemeketa Park MWC
report.sources_described: Surface water from Moody Gulch Creek (source 002_002; intake at the north entrance of Ogallala Warpath at Old Santa Cruz Hwy), treated by conventional surface water treatment. The company website adds that treated water from San Jose Water's Montevina Pipeline is a secondary source used only in emergencies.
violations: Lead Action Level Exceedance (Table 7, page 12): 'During September 2025, Chemeketa Park MWC collected 5 lead tap samples. One sample at 17708 Blackfoot Trail (9/24/2025) returned 36.4 µg/L, resulting in a 90th percentile of 18.2 µg/L, which exceeds the lead action level of 15 µg/L. A Tier 1 Public Notice was distributed to all customers on 11/19/2025. Follow-up samples collected on 11/25/2025 at the original exceedance site and the Tank Outlet (distribution system entry point) both returned 0.1 µg/L, well below the action level, indicating the exceedance was isolated to premise plumbing at one address and not systemic.' Duration: September-October 2025 monitoring period; continuing corrosion control evaluation and enhanced lead monitoring.

HAA5 MCL Violation (Table 7, page 13): 'On 11/19/2025, an HAA5 sample at 20891 Comanche Trail returned 195 µg/L (0.195 mg/L), exceeding the MCL of 60 µg/L (0.060 mg/L). A Citation and Compliance Order (No. 02_17_26J_005) was issued by the Division of Drinking Water on March 18, 2026.' Causes: naturally occurring organic matter (tannins) in the Moody Gulch source, elevated sodium hypochlorite dosage to maintain CT disinfection in cold weather, and increased water age at Comanche Trail. Duration November 2025 - ongoing; Tier 2 public notification; quarterly monitoring; Corrective Action Plan submitted June 2026; new 82,286-gallon contact-time tank installed April 2026; distribution flushing bi-weekly from April 2026, weekly from May 2026. Trend: 195 µg/L (Nov 2025), 102 µg/L (Feb 2026), 72 µg/L (May 2026).

TTHM MCL Violation (Table 7, page 14): 'On 11/19/2025, a TTHM sample at 20891 Comanche Trail returned 160 µg/L (0.160 mg/L), exceeding the MCL of 80 µg/L (0.080 mg/L).' Same causes and corrective actions as HAA5; duration November 2025 - ongoing. Trend: 160 µg/L (Nov 2025), 85 µg/L (Feb 2026), 82 µg/L (May 2026). 'Chemeketa Park MWC expects to return to full compliance by December 31, 2026.'

report.extraction_notes: No violations: report states 'Source water supplied to and distributed in the system met all EPA and State drinking water standards.' Table 1 (PDF pages 7-9, printed '1 of 3'..'3 of 3') is the backup well (-001), a disconnected source not used in 2025; Table 2 (PDF page 10) is the distribution system carrying SJWC Montevina water. Both tables have a single RESULT column headed '(ppm)' with no PHG column, so phg_printed is null throughout; units are ppm except Color (Units), Odor (T.O.N), pH (pH units), Turbidity (NTU), Gross Alpha (MCL cell says pCi/L) and Specific Conductivity (no unit printed). Several analytes list multiple dated results (2018-2025); every printed date/result line is kept as its own entry with sample_year set from the date, so the pipeline should prefer the latest sample_year per analyte. Superscript footnote markers on MCLs ('2' = secondary, '2a' = EPA secondary, 'a' = MCL no longer in effect) were dropped from mcl_printed and described in notes. The report prints Nitrite (as N) MCL as 10 and Nitrate+Nitrite (as N) MCL as 1, apparently swapped; copied as printed. Lead and copper in Table 2 are five individual tap results each (no 90th percentile), kept as five entries each. Hexavalent chromium result 0.00014 ppm (= 0.14 ppb) is dated 3/28/25. report.title: 2025 Water Quality Report - NASA Ames Research Center, Moffett Field, California (July 2026)
report.sources_described: Drinking water at NASA Ames is supplied by the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS), owned and operated by the SFPUC: Hetch Hetchy surface water (unfiltered; UV and chlorine disinfection, pH adjustment, fluoridation, chloramination) plus Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant filtered water; upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources and groundwater wells were not used in 2025, and the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Valley Water in April and May 2025. NASA Ames does not use groundwater.
violations: No exceedances of drinking water standards were identified in any of the samples collected at NASA Ames in 2025 (page 3; footnote 1: all results met State and Federal drinking water health standards).

Monitoring violation disclosed on behalf of the supplier (page 3): the San Francisco Regional Water System, operated by SFPUC, failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23, 2025 to July 2, 2025 because of a turbidimeter equipment failure; corrected July 3, 2025; the SFPUC states it was not an emergency and did not impact water quality.

Lead and copper tap monitoring (page 5, footnote 7): in the September 2023 round, 2 of 22 site samples (Buildings M583C and N200) had lead above the Action Level of 15 ppb; the 90th percentile (10.4 ppb) was below the AL so no regulatory violation occurred. N200 fountains are fitted with NSF/ANSI-certified lead-removing filters; M583C is abandoned and scheduled for demolition.
report.extraction_notes: Single supplier (SFPUC/SFRWS) so no per-source columns; the only source-specific rows are the three turbidity rows (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy vs. Filtered SVWTP water), which carry source_group. report.title: 2025 City of Milpitas Water Quality Report
report.sources_described: The City of Milpitas delivers treated water from two wholesale sources, the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC, Hetch Hetchy water combined with treated local water from Calaveras and San Antonio Reservoirs via the Sunol Valley WTP) and Valley Water (Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and local Anderson/Calero reservoir water treated at the Penitencia and Santa Teresa WTPs), both delivering treated surface water. violations: Page 1: 'In Calendar Year 2025, your water met all USEPA and State drinking water health standards. We are proud to report that our system had no water quality standard violations.'

Page 13 (printed 11), monitoring violation: 'We are required to monitor your drinking water for specific contaminants on a regular basis. Results of regular monitoring are an indicator of whether or not your drinking water meets health standards. During May 2025, we did not complete all monitoring for coliform bacteria, and therefore, cannot be sure of the quality of your drinking water during that time.'
report.extraction_notes: Data tables are on PDF pages 12-13 (printed page numbers 10-11; printed page n = PDF page n+2). Source-water rows have only Valley Water and SFPUC values; lead/copper, disinfectant residual, TTHM, HAA5 and total coliform are single distribution-system values (source_group 'Distribution System'). Where the Average cell is ND or '<x' but the Range has a numeric high, value = range high with value_basis 'range high', average null, detected true. ND, '<3', '<6', '<20', '<0.1' range-lows are recorded as 0 with the printed form in notes. MCL/AL/MRDL/ORL strings are copied as printed, including parentheses '(15)', brackets '[4]' and '1000 (NL)'. Specific conductance unit printed 'µS/cm', stored as 'uS/cm'. pH unit printed as a dash; SFPUC pH printed '-' and omitted. Lead 90th percentile printed as 0.0025 ppb (copied exactly; possibly a units slip in the report). Turbidity primary rows: Range column holds a percent-of-time figure, not a range. Uranium note e says radioactive monitoring is every nine years (detected 2013), so sample_year is null for uranium. PDF page 10 (printed 8, 'How to Read the Water Quality Table') shows a faded, cut-off sample table whose values differ from the 2025 table (e.g. Bromate 2.45 / 2.1c, Fluoride ND / 0.4, TOC 2.5 / 1.8, Turbidity 0.28 / 0.4c) and appears to be an earlier year's layout example; those rows were NOT extracted. report.title: Water Connection, July 2025 - Consumer Confidence Report (2025 Report to Consumers on Water Quality)
report.sources_described: Morgan Hill is in South Santa Clara County between the Coyote and Llagas underground aquifers, which are the source of its water supply. The City has 16 active groundwater wells that supplied 2.33 billion gallons in 2025 to about 15,306 connections; the water is disinfected with sodium hypochlorite.
report.extraction_notes: Cover is titled 'July 2025' but the body is the '2025 Report to Consumers on Water Quality' covering January 1 - December 31, 2025 (published 2026), so data_year is 2025. Data tables span pages 6 (microbiological, lead/copper, school lead, sodium/hardness) and 7 (primary, disinfection byproducts/chlorine, SOC, secondary, additional constituents, PFAS); page assignment verified against rendered images because pdftotext bled page-7 text onto page 6. The report prints 0 rather than ND for non-detects (arsenic, 1,2,3-TCP, turbidity, lead 90th percentile, and all range lows for TTHM/HAA5/barium/PFAS); zeros are copied as printed, with detected=false only where every printed figure is 0. Units copied verbatim: mg/L vs mg/l, ug/L vs µg/L, umho/cm, 'UNITS' for turbidity, 'unit' for pH, grains/gal (printed GRAINS/GAL). PFAS and lithium are 2024 samples reported in ug/L (pipeline must convert to ppt). 1,2,3-TCP MCL/PHG printed as 0 and the arsenic PHG printed as 5 are copied as printed. Nitrate is reported as N with MCL 10 (the 2024 edition used as-NO3 / 45). No violations: 'For the calendar year 2025, your tap water met all U.S. EPA and State drinking water health standards' and the system is 'in full compliance'; all 'Exceeded MCL?' cells read NO/NS. Text verified against rendered images of pages 6 and 7.

report.title: City of Mountain View 2025 Water Quality Report (Consumer Confidence Report, June 2026)
report.sources_described: The City purchases approximately 90 percent of its drinking water from the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC) Regional Water System, mostly Sierra Nevada snowmelt stored in Hetch Hetchy Reservoir plus runoff from Alameda, San Mateo and Santa Clara county watersheds; approximately 8 percent is treated surface water purchased from Valley Water (Rinconada Water Treatment Plant; South Bay Aqueduct, Dyer Reservoir, Lake Del Valle, San Luis Reservoir and Calero Reservoir); two percent comes from City-owned groundwater wells in the lower aquifer of the Santa Clara subbasin, blended with SFPUC water and also serving as emergency backup.
report.extraction_notes: Report covers January-December 2025; states 'In 2025, Mountain View's drinking water met all Federal and State standards' and has no violations section. All data tables are on PDF page 5, which is a two-page spread (printed pages 5 and 6). The source-water table ('CITY OF MOUNTAIN VIEW SOURCE WATER QUALITY DATA FOR 2025') has three source column groups: 'SFPUC' (Range + 'Avg. or [Max]'), 'Valley Water' (Range + 'Avg. or [Max]') and 'CMV Wells' (Range only, footnote 2); one entry per analyte per column, named in source_group. Cells printed '-' (Non Applicable / not reported for that source) were skipped rather than given empty entries; e.g. Barium has CMV Wells data only, Gross Alpha/Uranium have Valley Water and (gross alpha) CMV Wells only, Chlorate SFPUC only. A separate 'MOUNTAIN VIEW DRINKING WATER (1)' table (distribution system: turbidity, TTHMs, HAA-5s, fluoride, total chlorine, free ammonia, customer-tap lead and copper) has a single 'Range or [Avg]' column; source_group = 'Mountain View Drinking Water (distribution system)'. Values printed in square brackets are maxima or averages per the column header ('[Max]'/'[Avg]'). Range lows printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as 0 with the printed form kept in notes; averages printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as null with range high used as value and detected=true because the range shows a detection. Bracketed MCL column entries ('[1000]', '[800]', '[50]', '[15]', '[1.3]') are notification levels or action levels as printed; 'NS' = No Standard. The report prints a DLR column; numeric DLRs are kept in notes. Sample year is 2025 per the table title except Valley Water radionuclides (footnote 10: last tested 2022) and the CMV Wells gross alpha (year not printed). No PFAS table row exists; the page-4 statement (no PFAS detected, most recent test 2023) is recorded as a flagged text-only entry. The HAA-5 running-annual-average range high (63.0 ppb) is printed above the 60 ppb MCL while footnote (1) says all results met standards; recorded as printed. Downloaded from the Wayback Machine snapshot of the city's own URL because mountainview.gov returns Akamai 403 to this host.

report.title: Our Water, Our Future: City of Palo Alto 2025 Water Quality Report (City of Palo Alto Utilities 2025 Annual Water Quality Report)
report.sources_described: Palo Alto's water is delivered by the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS, operated by the SFPUC); the major source is Sierra Nevada snowmelt flowing down the Tuolumne River to Hetch Hetchy Reservoir (unfiltered, UV and chlorine disinfected, pH adjusted, fluoridated and chloraminated), supplemented by local reservoirs in Alameda County treated at the Sunol Valley WTP and San Mateo County reservoirs treated at the Harry Tracy WTP. In 2025 neither the SFRWS upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources nor its groundwater wells were used; the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Santa Clara Valley Water District in April and May.
violations: NOTICE FROM THE SAN FRANCISCO PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION (SFPUC) (p. 4): the SFRWS, operated by the SFPUC, failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (SVWTP) from June 23, 2025, to July 2, 2025. This monitoring violation was the result of equipment failure (the turbidimeter was not operating) and was corrected on July 3, 2025. The notice states the failure was not an emergency, did not impact water quality, and that during the period the water delivered to Palo Alto customers met all federal and state drinking water standards; operations staff were retrained and additional operational and maintenance activities implemented to prevent recurrence.
report.extraction_notes: Report covers calendar year 2025 and states Palo Alto's water meets all federal and state drinking water standards (footnote 1: all results met state and federal drinking water health standards). Data tables are on PDF pages 6 ('Your Water Quality Data for 2025': DETECTED CONTAMINANTS and NON-REGULATED WATER QUALITY PARAMETERS) and 7 (CONSTITUENTS WITH SECONDARY STANDARDS and LEAD AND COPPER). There are no per-source columns: all rows are a single SFRWS/SFPUC system column, so source_group is null throughout; turbidity is instead split into rows per treatment source (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy Water, Filtered Water from SVWTP, Filtered Water from HTWTP), kept in raw_name. The DETECTED CONTAMINANTS table has one combined column 'Average or [Max]': bracketed values are maxima or highest (locational) running annual averages per footnotes 3-4 and are stored with value_basis 'max' or 'highest running annual average' and average=null; unbracketed values are averages. Range lows printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as 0 with the printed form in notes; averages printed 'ND' or '<2' are stored as null with range high used as value. Copper is printed in ppb (RAL 1300, PHG 300) and lead 90th percentile is printed as 0 although individual samples ranged 0.2 - 9.74 ppb; lead/copper sampling year is 2023 (footnotes 6-7). E. coli printed [0] positive samples is recorded as detected=false. Cryptosporidium is discussed in text only (found at very low levels in source and treated water in 2025, no numbers), so no entry. The report lists no PFAS, radiological or UCMR rows. The PDF was obtained through the WebFetch service because paloalto.gov returns Akamai 403 to direct curl from this host; sha256 is of the saved file.

report.title: 2025 Water Quality Consumer Confidence Report (Published June 2026)
report.sources_described: Three sources used interchangeably or blended, averaging 15 million gallons per day: the City's system of 20 active deep groundwater wells (500–900 ft aquifers; most of the water), SFPUC Hetch Hetchy System water (snowmelt from the Northern Sierra Nevada; typically serves the area north of Highway 101; fluoridated, blended with unfluoridated well water in 95054), and Valley Water treated surface water from the Rinconada Water Treatment Plant (Calero Reservoir and Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta imports; primarily the south-west portion of the City).
violations: Tier 3 Notice from SFPUC (PDF page 5): because of equipment failure, the San Francisco Regional Water System operated by the SFPUC did not monitor recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23 to July 2, 2025; corrected July 3, 2025; no emergency or impact to SFPUC's water quality.

Lead: 'No Santa Clara water sources have exceeded the ACTION LEVEL for lead' (p.5); 2022 residential tap sampling 0 exceedances. In the 2018 school lead testing (33 schools, 172 samples) one sample exceeded the AL: John Sutter Elementary 26 ppb; repeat sampling after plumbing repairs was non-detect (table note 6).
Report states all water meets applicable federal and state drinking-water standards; no MCL violations disclosed.
report.extraction_notes: All table rows are on PDF page 4 of the 6-page report (the same table is also published as a separate 1-page accessible PDF, saved alongside and used to cross-check). Source-water table columns: 'Analysis for CSC WELL WATER', 'Analysis for VALLEY WATER', 'Analysis for SFPUC' (source_group values copied in the printed capitalisation), each with Range and Average; the SFPUC header adds '[highest running average]'. Distribution-system tables (coliform, E. coli, TTHM, HAA5, chlorine residual, lead/copper, lithium) have no source column -> source_group null; their second standards column is headed 'State MCL' (holds PHG/MRDLG-like values 0.3, 0.2, 4), stored in phg_printed where it is a goal and nulled for coliform (5.0%). Cells printed 'NA' produced no entry (listed in the notes of the sibling entries). Where the average is printed 'ND' but the range shows a detection ('ND - x'), the entry is detected=true with value=range_high and average=null; ranges 'ND - x' use range_low 0. Values printed with '<' (e.g. '< 3 - 11', '<5', '< 20') are below reporting limits: a '<x' range low is stored as x with a note; a row printed entirely '<x' is treated as not detected. Units copied as printed in upper case (PPM, PPB, UNITS). Foaming agents (MBAS) printed in PPB with values 0.022/0.014 against MCL 500 (probably ppm values; copied as printed). Lithium table range 'ND - 10' conflicts with the p.5 narrative that no lithium was detected. Lead/copper residential taps sampled in 2022 (sample_year 2022); school lead testing 2018; all other rows default to sample_year 2025 although the report notes some data may be more than one year old. PFAS entries (page 5) come from the UCMR5 narrative statement, not table rows, and are flagged in notes. Only constituents detected in at least one source appear in the report's table.

report.sources_described: All of the current drinking water supply comes from the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS), wholesaled by the SFPUC: surface water stored in reservoirs in the Sierra Nevada (Hetch Hetchy, unfiltered but UV/chlorine disinfected, pH adjusted, fluoridated and chloraminated), Alameda County and San Mateo County, with local Bay Area reservoir water treated at the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (page 2). report.title: City of San José 2025 Water Quality Report (San José Municipal Water System)
report.sources_described: North San José and Alviso receive a blend of Hetch Hetchy water and treated water (Alameda watershed reservoirs treated at the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant) purchased from the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission; in 2025 groundwater from local deep-water wells in North San José supplemented the SFPUC supply, so some customers received a blend of groundwater and SFPUC water.
report.extraction_notes: Single 2025 report for the whole San José Municipal Water System (PWSIDs CA4310019 North San José/Alviso and CA4310020 Evergreen/Edenvale/Coyote Valley); the same PDF is saved under both reports/ directories and this JSON contains only the columns for this PWSID. The one data table is on PDF page 5 (printed as the back inside panel of the brochure) with six source columns, each with Average and Range sub-columns: 'Evergreen (Valley Water Treated Water)', 'Evergreen (Groundwater)', 'Edenvale* (Groundwater)', 'Coyote Valley** (Groundwater)', 'North San José/Alviso (SFPUC Treated Water)', 'North San José/Alviso (Groundwater)'; source_group = column name (asterisks dropped; they refer to the temporary-chlorination footnotes). Cells printed NA (not applicable) have no entry. Lead and Copper are printed once across the Evergreen/Edenvale/Coyote Valley columns and once across the North San José/Alviso columns (90th percentile, number of samples exceeding AL, 2024 customer-tap data). Sample year is 2025 (table titled '2025 Water Quality Data') except footnote a cells (superscript a = distribution system data in 2023) and footnote e lead/copper (2024). Where the Average cell is ND but the Range has a numeric high, value = range high (value_basis 'range_high', average null). MCL/PHG strings are copied as printed including '(4)'/'[4]' (MRDL/MRDLG), '[15]'/'[1300]' (AL) and '(0)' (MCLG). Total Coliform has a blank unit cell and 'Highest %'/'Range' sub-headers; recorded as % with value = highest monthly %. Turbidity appears three times: 'Turbidity (unfiltered sources)' and 'Turbidity (filtered sources)' in the Clarity section (printed as 'Highest Level = x') and a secondary-standard 'Turbidity' row. Anomalies copied as printed: Iron row unit 'ppm' with SMCL 0.3 but SFPUC values 18 / ND - 36 (almost certainly ppb); Potassium North San José/Alviso (Groundwater) average '16' with range 1.4 - 1.8. The report has no violations section; its only compliance statements are 'a reliable water supply that meets or exceeds all drinking water health standards' (p.6) and footnote d 'All filtered water sources met this standard'. Typical-source codes (last column) were not transcribed. This file holds the North San José/Alviso (SFPUC Treated Water) and North San José/Alviso (Groundwater) columns and the North San José/Alviso lead and copper cell. SFPUC HAA5 range high 63 ppb is above the 60 ppb MCL as a single result while the printed average (running average, footnote b) is 42; the report declares no violation.

report.title: Purissima Hills Water District - Water Quality 2025 Annual Report
report.sources_described: All water is San Francisco Regional Water System (SFPUC) surface water stored in reservoirs in the Sierra Nevada (Hetch Hetchy, unfiltered but UV/chlorine disinfected, pH adjusted, fluoridated and chloraminated), Alameda County and San Mateo County; local Alameda County reservoir water is treated at the Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant. In 2025 neither the SFRWS upcountry non-Hetch Hetchy sources nor its groundwater wells were used, but the SFRWS imported a very small amount (0.38%) of treated water from Valley Water in April and May (page 8).
violations: Page 4, 'Notification of Process Monitoring Violation': the SFRWS failed to monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant from June 23, 2025 to July 2, 2025. The monitoring violation was the result of equipment failure and was corrected on July 3, 2025; it was not an emergency and did not impact water quality.
Page 2: '100% Compliance with drinking water standards'. Table footnote 1 (page 7): 'All results met State and Federal drinking water health standards.'
report.extraction_notes: Tables on pages 6-7 are 'detected contaminants' only (single system-wide set of values, no per-source columns). The TURBIDITY section is split by source as rows (Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy Water; Filtered Water from SVWTP), so those entries carry the row label in source_group; all other entries have source_group null. Most values are SFPUC regional system results; lead/copper are PHWD tap samples from September 2023 (footnotes 6-7) and the next LCR round is 2026. Two extra entries are not table rows: treated-water fluoride from footnote 4 and the 'No PFAS Detected' statement from page 4. Convention: a range printed 'ND - x' or '<n - x' is stored range_low 0 / range_high x (the printed string is kept in notes). Rows whose Average (or 90th percentile) is printed 'ND' or '<n' but whose range shows a detection are stored value null, average null, detected true, value_basis 'average (printed ND)' - nothing is substituted for the unprintable average. Rows printed ND with no range are detected false. 'sample_year' is the latest year when the report prints a year range; the printed range is in notes.

entries.notes: TURBIDITY section, row 'Unfiltered Hetch Hetchy Water'. Range 0.3 - 0.5 are monthly average turbidity values measured every 4 hours daily at Tesla Treatment Facilities (footnote 2); [3.4] is the maximum.

report.title: 2025 Consumer Confidence Report (CCR)
report.sources_described: Groundwater only: 'All of our water is pumped from 22 wells (not surface water) located throughout our service area', drawn from the aquifers underlying the Santa Clara Valley (page 5).
violations: Every data row prints Violation 'NO'; the report has no violations section and states the water 'is safe, clean and great tasting' and that the report lists only contaminants detected in samples (pages 1, 4).

Observation, not declared by the report: UCMR 5 well-sample PFOS average .0046 ppb is above the MCL .0040 ppb printed in the same table (page 4). The report says: 'These unregulated contaminants did not have a drinking water standard set by the USEPA at the time of sampling ... Since sampling, the USEPA has set standards for some of the PFOS constituents as noted by the MCLs posted in the table above.'
report.extraction_notes: Single-source (groundwater) system; tables have one results column, so source_group is null throughout. The report's results column is headed 'Amount Detected' (or 'Detected') with a separate 'Range Low-High' column; Amount Detected is treated as the average (value_basis 'average', average filled) except where the row itself names another basis (90th percentile for lead/copper, annual running average for free chlorine, highest monthly percent positive for total coliform). Leading-dot numbers (.15, .11, .0027, .38, .015, .23, .0046) are stored as decimals; ND range-lows are stored as 0. PFHxS average is printed ',0073' (comma) and stored as 0.0073. Iron is printed in ppm (SMCL 0.3 ppm) and lead/copper in ppm; units are kept as printed. pH has no printed unit. Specific conductance unit printed 'µS/cm', stored as 'uS/cm'. Disinfection by-products appear in two sub-tables: 'Calero Pressure Zone Only' (TTHM, HAA, free chlorine; Range 'None') on page 2 and per-site rows (#4, #5, #9, #10, #17, #18 TTHM/HAA) on page 3; each row is a separate entry with the site in raw_name/notes. The 'Other Substances' table (alkalinity, bicarbonate, calcium, hardness, magnesium, potassium, sodium) has no MCL/PHG columns. Lead and copper were sampled in 2023 (year printed in the table); all other rows 2025. No E. coli, radon, VOC, or secondary manganese/zinc rows are printed (report lists detected contaminants only).
